source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when Yeshua{H3442} was born{H3205} in Beit Lechem{H1035} of Yehudah{H3063}, in the days{H3117} of Herod the king{H4428}, behold{H2009}, gazers{H2374} at the stars{H3556} came{H935} from the east{H4217} to Yerushalayim{H3389},

one_way_hebrew: חוזים בכוכבים — 'gazers at the stars': Isaiah's exact phrase for Babylon's astrologers, החזים בכוכבים (Isa 47:13). Greek μάγοι transliterates a Persian title and explains nothing; the Hebrew names the visitors from the east in the east's own biblical vocabulary — the taunt-word of the oracle against Babylon.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק שלישי (Perek 3) begins here.
The transcriber's footnote records that the ms writes the name both plain (הורודוס) and as a marked transliteration (הורוד״וס, so at 2:15, 19).
Howard's apparatus (2:1): יהודה] יודא BDEFG; והנה] + מאגוש A (the Greek 'magos' written into ms A — the foreign word entering the tradition, not leaving it).

verses.translation: saying{H559}: Where{H346} is the king{H4428} of the Yehudim{H3064} who has been born{H3205}? We have seen{H7200} his star in the east{H4217}, and with valuable{H2803} gifts{H4979} have come{H935} to bow down{H7812} to him.

greek_deviations: The gifts stand inside the question itself — 'with valuable gifts we have come to bow down to him' — where Greek keeps them for v. 11. The Hebrew magi announce homage-with-tribute at the gate.
translation_notes: סבבו — the base ms's word, literally 'his circling/circuit' (from סבב); all other mss read 'his star' (ככבו BCDFG, כוכבו D; A ככבים 'stars'), and Howard prints '(his star)'. The base may preserve an idiom for the star's course; the translation follows the sense.
באו — 'they have come' (third person inside their own speech); ms A smooths to ובאנו ('and we have come'), and Howard supplies '(we)'.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:2): סבבו] ככבים A, ככבו BCDFG, כוכבו D; הנולד] + אשר G; ובמתנות חשובות באו] ובאנו במתנות חשובות A.

verses.translation: And Herod the king{H4428} heard{H8085}, and he was terrified{H926}, and all{H3605} the inhabitants{H3427} of Yerushalayim{H3389} with him.

one_way_hebrew: ויבהל (H926) — the dismay-word of Gen 45:3 (נבהלו מפניו — the brothers terrified before Joseph) and the root of 24:6 (תבהלו). Greek ἐταράχθη ('stirred up') is weaker than the Hebrew's terror.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:3): ושמע] וישמע A.

verses.translation: And he gathered{H6908} all{H3605} his great ones{H1419} and inquired{H1245} of them if they knew{H3045} in what{H335} place{H4725} the Mashiach{H4899} would be born{H3205}.

greek_deviations: 'He gathered all HIS GREAT ONES' (גדוליו) — Greek specifies 'all the chief priests and scribes of the people.' The other mss expand toward the Greek in five different directions (A 'the great ones of the wise men, the priests and the scribes'; B 'great ones and wise men and scribes'; G 'the wise men and the scribes'...) — divergent expansions of a short original, the classic signature of the base reading being prior.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:4): גדוליו] גדולי החכמים הכהנים והסופרים A, גדלים וחכמים וסופרים B, גדוליהם החכמים והסופרים D, גדוליהם החכמים E, גדולי החכמים והסופרים F, החכמים והסופרים G; נולד] יולד ABDEF, יולד ישו G; כל omitted in G.

verses.translation: And they answered{H6030} him: In Beit Lechem{H1035} Yehudah{H3063}, as it is written{H3789} by the mouth{H6310} of the prophet{H5030}:

one_way_hebrew: ככתיב — the rabbinic citation formula ('as it is written'); ms A has the Aramaic דכתיב, the Talmud's own form. Citation formulas are the most habitual part of a writer's hand: this hand cites like a rabbi, not like a translator of γέγραπται.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:5): יהודה] יודא BDEFG; ככתיב] דכתיב A.

verses.translation: And you{H859}, Beit Lechem{H1035} Yehudah{H3063}, Ephrathah{H672}, land{H776} of Yehudah: behold{H2005}, you are little{H6810} among the thousands{H505} of Yehudah — from you shall come forth{H3318} for me one to be ruler{H4910} in Israel{H3478}.

one_way_hebrew: The quotation is Micah 5:1 as the Hebrew Bible reads it — אפרתה, צעיר, באלפי יהודה, ממך לי יצא, מושל — Micah's own consonants. Greek Matthew rewrites the verse: it drops 'Ephrathah,' inserts 'by NO MEANS least' (οὐδαμῶς ἐλαχίστη — reversing Micah's point), and turns 'thousands' (אלפי) into 'princes' (ἡγεμόσιν, reading אלופי), diverging from both the Hebrew and the LXX. The Shem Tov text quotes Micah; a back-translation from Greek Matthew would have reproduced Greek Matthew's altered quotation instead. And the proof of direction stands in the apparatus: mss BDEFG read אין ('you are NOT little'), assimilating toward the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:6): הן] אין BDEFG; יהודה (2nd, 3rd)] יודא DEFG; להיות omitted in D.

verses.translation: Then{H227} king{H4428} Herod called{H7121} the diviners{H7080} in secret{H5643} and asked{H7592} them well{H3190} the time{H2165} the star{H3556} appeared{H7200} to them.

one_way_hebrew: קוסמים (H7080) — the Torah's category for diviners (Deut 18:10, קסם קסמים; Josh 13:22, Balaam הקוסם). The narrative began with Isaiah's חוזים בכוכבים (v. 1) and now uses the Torah's קוסמים: two native biblical terms where Greek repeats the one Persian loanword μάγοι. A Hebrew author varies inside his own lexicon; a translator tracks his source's single word.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:7): להם omitted in EF; המלך הורודוס] transposed EF; ראית] נראה D.

verses.translation: And he sent them{H7971} to Beit Lechem{H1035} and said{H559} to them: Go{H1980} and inquire{H7592} well{H3190} concerning{H1157} the child{H3206}, and when you find{H4672} him, tell{H5046} me — and I also will come{H935} to him to bow down{H7812}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:8): אליהם] להם AF; הילד] הנולד F; לי] אלי A; אליו להשתחוות] להשתחוות לו G.

verses.translation: And they listened{H8085} to the king{H4428} and went{H1980}; and behold{H2009}, the star{H3556} which they saw{H7200} in the east{H4217} was going{H1980} before them{H6440} until they came{H935} to the place{H4725}. And when they entered Beit Lechem{H1035}, it stood{H5975} opposite{H5048} the place where the child{H3206} was.

one_way_hebrew: הולך לפניהם — 'going before them': the pillar's own verbs (Exod 13:21, ויהוה הלך לפניהם... לנחתם הדרך — 'YHWH went before them... to lead them the way'). The star escorts the seekers as the pillar escorted Israel; the Hebrew reader hears the Exodus guide behind the Gentiles' star.
translation_notes: וילכו — the circulating transcription doubles the vav (וילכוו); the scan reads וילכו, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:9): אל המלך] אליו E, לו F.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when they saw{H7200} the star{H3556}, they rejoiced{H8055} a great{H1419} joy{H8057}, exceedingly{H3966}.

one_way_hebrew: שמחו שמחה גדולה — the cognate-accusative of Jonah 4:6 (וישמח... שמחה גדולה) and 1 Kgs 1:40. Greek ἐχάρησαν χαρὰν μεγάλην carries the Semitic figure so literally that the Greek itself has always read as translation-Greek — here stands the Hebrew it translates.

verses.translation: And they came{H935} into the house{H1004} and found him{H4672} with Miryam{H4813} his mother{H517}, and they knelt{H3766} before him{H6440} and bowed down{H7812} to him; and they opened{H6605} their sacks{H572} and brought{H935} him an offering{H4503} of gold{H2091} and frankincense{H3828} and myrrh{H4753} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, mira.

one_way_hebrew: אמתחותיהם (H572) — 'their SACKS': amtachat lives in exactly one place in Scripture — the Joseph narrative (Gen 42-44, fifteen times), the brothers' grain-sacks with the treasure returned in their mouths. Treasure carried into Egypt-ward exile in an אמתחת is a Joseph-cycle image, and this chapter is already running on the Joseph pattern (dreams, flight to Egypt). Greek θησαυρούς ('treasure-chests') loses the word and the echo.

מנחת זהב ולבונה — the gifts are called a מנחה, the Temple's tribute-offering — and frankincense upon the minchah is the Torah's own prescription (Lev 2:1-2: ונתן עליה לבנה). In Hebrew the magi present the offering of Lev 2; in Greek they merely 'offer gifts.'

The scribe glosses מור with the Latin: בלעז מי״רא (myrrha) — a Hebrew text annotated with church vocabulary for readers in a Latin land, like קריס״טוס (1:16) and מאריטמה (4:13). The gloss points from Hebrew outward.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:11): ויביאו] ויבאו ADEF, ויבואו BCG; בלעז מירא omitted in EF. Howard's printed text points the loanword (מִי״רָא); the points are stripped here, as with all pointed name-forms.
The transcription drops the aleph of the second ויביאו; the scan reads ויביאו, corrected here.

verses.translation: And they were commanded{H6680} in a dream{H2472} — by the messenger{H4397} who spoke{H559} to them — not to return{H7725} to Herod, and they turned{H6437} the way{H1870} of their land{H776} by a different{H312} road.

translation_notes: The base syntax is rough — מהמלאך אמר להם trails the command; mss ABDEFG smooth both halves (מהמלאך לבילתי שוב אל הורודוס; ויפנו דרך אחרת ללכת אל ארצם). The rough reading is the harder and older one.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:12): לבלתי . . . להם] מהמלאך לבילתי שוב אל הורודוס ABDEFG; ויפנו . . . אחרת] ויפנו דרך אחרת ללכת אל ארצם ABDEFG.

verses.translation: As they were going{H1980}, behold{H2009}, the messenger{H4397} of YHWH{H3068} appeared{H7200} to Yoseph{H3130}: Arise{H6965}, take{H3947} the boy{H5288} and his mother{H517} and flee{H1272} to Egypt{H4714}, and stay{H5975} there until{H5704} I tell{H559} you — for Herod will seek{H1245} the boy to kill{H2026} him.

one_way_hebrew: המה הולכים — the participial scene-opener of biblical narrative (2 Kgs 2:11, ויהי המה הלכים הלוך ודבר). קום... וברח — Rivkah's flight-command to Yaakov verbatim in form (Gen 27:43, וקום ברח לך). And the child is הנער — the na'ar of the patriarch narratives (Gen 21:12-20; 22:5,12) — where Greek repeats παιδίον.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק רביעי (Perek 4) begins here.
First occurrence of ה״ in this chapter — the ms writes the Name as ה״ ('The Name'); see 1:22.
The transcription reads ובקש for the scan's יבקש; corrected.
Howard's apparatus (2:13): נראה] + בחלום DGH ('in a dream'); אל יוסף] ליוסף EF; יוסף] + לאמר DG; אליך] + לפי שעתיד DG; את הנער להרוג] להרוג את הנער ABCDEF, להרוג את ישו הנער G.

verses.translation: And he took{H3947} the boy{H5288} and his mother{H517}.

greek_deviations: The verse is bare: 'And he took the boy and his mother' — no 'by night,' no 'departed into Egypt' (Greek: παρέλαβεν... νυκτὸς καὶ ἀνεχώρησεν εἰς Αἴγυπτον). Ms A adds בלילה וילך למצרים and DG add בלילה וירד מצרימה — two independent retro-fits toward the Greek, marking the short text as the base.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:14): Beginning] + ויקם D(margin)G; אמו] + בלילה וילך למצרים A, + בלילה וירד מצרימה DG.

verses.translation: And he was{H1961} there{H8033} until{H5704} Herod died{H4191}, to complete{H1584} what was spoken{H559} by the mouth{H6310} of the prophet{H5030}: And out of Egypt{H4714} I called{H7121} my son{H1121}.

one_way_hebrew: ממצרים קראתי לבני — Hos 11:1 in Hosea's own consonants: 'out of Egypt I called MY SON' (singular). The LXX reads 'his CHILDREN' (τὰ τέκνα αὐτοῦ); Greek Matthew's τὸν υἱόν μου agrees with the Hebrew of Hosea against the LXX — Greek Matthew's maker had to reach past his Greek Bible to the Hebrew here. The Shem Tov text does not reach; it simply IS the Hebrew, word for word.
textual_notes: The ms writes the name with the transliteration mark here: הורוד״וס (so again v. 19).

verses.translation: Then{H227} Herod saw{H7200} that the diviners{H7080} had mocked him, and it was grievous{H7489} to him exceedingly{H3966}, and he was grieved{H6087} to his heart{H3820}; and he commanded{H6680} and sent{H7971} to all his princes{H8269} to kill{H2026} all the children{H3206} in Beit Lechem{H1035} and its borders{H1366} who were born{H3205} from the time{H2165} the diviners had told{H559} him the boy{H5288} was born.

one_way_hebrew: ויתעצב אל לבו — Gen 6:6's exact phrase, ויתעצב אל לבו ('and he was grieved to his heart'): the grief of God before the flood, here on the lips of the narrative for the tyrant grieving over a spoiled deception — a bitter Genesis echo carried in four consonant-groups. Greek ἐθυμώθη λίαν ('he raged greatly') is a different emotion and carries no allusion; only the Hebrew can quote Genesis.
greek_deviations: The base lacks 'from two years old and under': the decree runs from the time the diviners named. Mss DH add משני שנים ולמטה הנולדים and G משני שנים ולמטה כפי הזמן — assimilations to the Greek.
לכל שריו — 'to all his PRINCES' (שרים): Herod kills through his officers, stated plainly; Greek's ἀποστείλας ('having sent') leaves the agents unnamed.
translation_notes: שראו — the base ms reads 'that they had SEEN him' (a near-dittograph after ראה); mss DGH read שלעגו ('had MOCKED him'), which the sense requires — Howard prints '(mocked)'. The translation follows the variant; the words preserve the ms.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק חמישי (Perek 5) begins here.
The transcription reads שלולד for the scan's שנולד; corrected.
Howard's apparatus (2:16): שראו] שלעגו DGH; מזמן] + משני שנים ולמטה הנולדים DH, + משני שנים ולמטה כפי הזמן G; ויצו וישלח] transposed ADEFG; לכל (2nd)] את כל D.

verses.translation: Then{H227} was completed{H7999} the word{H1697} which Yirmeyah{H3414} the prophet{H5030} spoke:

one_way_hebrew: נשלם — 'was made whole' (שלם): a third native fulfillment verb in two chapters (לגמור 1:22; 2:15; לקיים 2:23) where Greek has the one word πληρόω throughout. Living Hebrew varies; translation tracks.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:17): מה omitted in ABDEFGH; הנביא omitted in FH.

verses.translation: A voice{H6963} is heard{H8085} in Ramah{H7414} — lamentation{H5092}, bitter{H8563} weeping{H1065} — Rachel{H7354} weeping{H1058} for her children{H1121}, and so on.

one_way_hebrew: The quotation is Jer 31:15 letter for letter — קול ברמה נשמע נהי בכי תמרורים רחל מבכה על בניה — and then it simply stops: וכו׳ ('etc.'). A scribe writing for readers who carry Jeremiah in their memory cites the opening and waves at the rest; Greek Matthew must write the verse out in full, and does. No translator FROM Greek puts 'etc.' in the middle of his source's quotation — the abbreviation is the fingerprint of a Hebrew book among Hebrew readers (the same hand: ע״כ at 3:12, וגו׳ at 4:4 and 4:6).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:18): נהי omitted in G; בניה] + מאנה להנחם על בניה כי איננו A (ms A copies on into the verse's next clause).

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961}, when Herod the king{H4428} died{H4191}, the messenger{H4397} of YHWH{H3068} appeared{H7200} in a dream{H2472} to Yoseph{H3130} in Egypt{H4714},

translation_notes: בחלום — the transcription reads מחלום; the scan reads בחלום, corrected here.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:19): המלך omitted in ABDEFG.

verses.translation: saying{H559}: Arise{H6965}, take{H3947} the boy{H5288} and his mother{H517} and go{H1980} to the Land of Israel, for those who sought{H1245} the boy to put him to death{H4191} have died{H4191}.

one_way_hebrew: כי מתו המבקשים... — the sentence spoken to Moshe in Midian, Exod 4:19: לך שב מצרים כי מתו כל האנשים המבקשים את נפשך ('go, return to Egypt, for all the men who sought your life are dead') — same command-form, same reason-clause, the direction reversed. The Redeemer's childhood is written across Moshe's: in Hebrew the sentence is recognizably the Torah's own; Greek τεθνήκασιν οἱ ζητοῦντες is its translation.
textual_notes: The ms writes א״י — the scribal abbreviation of ארץ ישראל ('the Land of Israel') — here and in v. 21: the everyday shorthand of a Hebrew scribe.
Howard's apparatus (2:20): את הנער להמית] transposed/reworded in A (להרוג את הנער), BDG, EF.

verses.translation: And he arose{H6965} and took{H3947} the boy{H5288} and his mother{H517}, and they returned{H7725} to the Land of Israel.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:21): אל א״י] לא״י ABDEFG.

verses.translation: And he heard{H8085} that Horqanos — his name{H8034} is Argelaus — reigned{H4427} in Yehudah{H3063} in place{H8478} of Herod his father{H1}, and he feared{H3372} to go{H1980} there; and the messenger{H4397} urged him in a dream{H2472}, and he turned{H6437} to the land{H776} of Gilgal{H1537}.

greek_deviations: Two readings no Greek text carries: (1) the new ruler is called הורקנוס — 'Hyrcanus,' the Hasmonean royal name — with Archelaus given as the gloss ('his name is Argelaus'): a naming that only makes sense inside Jewish historical memory, where 'Hyrcanus' is what a Judean client-king is called; (2) Yoseph turns to 'the land of GILGAL' (הגלגל) where Greek has Galilee — and the same reading returns at 4:12. Gilgal, the Jordan camp of Josh 4-5, is no translator's slip twice over; ms B normalizes both to הגליל.
translation_notes: ויזרזהו — zeraz, the rabbinic verb 'to urge on' (no biblical Strong's): 'the messenger URGED him,' where Greek has the passive 'being warned in a dream.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:22): וישמע] ונשמע DG; ביהודה] ביודא BF, omit D; שמו] + בלעז B, לעז A ('in the foreign tongue'); בחלום] + לאמר A; הגלגל] הגליל B.

verses.translation: And he came{H935} and dwelt{H7931} in the city{H5892} called{H7121} Nazarit, to establish{H6965} what the prophet{H5030} said: He shall be called{H7121} Nazaret.

one_way_hebrew: The fulfillment only sounds in Hebrew: behind נאזרת stand נצר — the Branch of Isa 11:1 (ונצר משרשיו יפרה) — and נזיר, the consecrated one (Judg 13:5,7). Greek Ναζωραῖος κληθήσεται has puzzled Greek readers ever since, because the prophet-word it appeals to is a Hebrew consonant-play; in this text the pun is at home.
לקיים מה שאמר — the rabbinic fulfillment formula (לקיים מה שנאמר), the standard citation form of the midrash; a fourth fulfillment idiom in two chapters (see 2:17).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (2:23): נאזרית] נזרות A, נזראת B, נאזרת CDG, נאזראת EF; הנביא] + כי A.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 2 in the Shem Tov Hebrew quotes the prophets in their own consonants and tells the story in the Torah's idioms. (1) 2:6 gives Micah 5:1 as Micah wrote it — אפרתה, 'you are LITTLE among the THOUSANDS of Yehudah' — where Greek Matthew rewrites the verse ('by no means least... among the princes'); mss BDEFG assimilate toward the Greek (אין 'not little'), showing the direction of change. (2) 2:15 gives Hos 11:1 verbatim ('out of Egypt I called MY SON') — the reading Greek Matthew itself takes from the Hebrew against the LXX's 'his children.' (3) 2:18 quotes Jer 31:15 letter for letter and breaks off with וכו׳ ('etc.') — a scribe citing for readers who know the rest by heart; the same habit closes 3:12 (ע״כ) and 4:4/4:6 (וגו׳). (4) The star-seekers are named twice in native terms — Isaiah's חוזים בכוכבים (Isa 47:13) and the Torah's קוסמים (Deut 18:10) — where Greek repeats the one loanword μάγοι. (5) 2:16 grieves Herod in Gen 6:6's exact phrase (ויתעצב אל לבו) and lacks 'from two years old and under' (supplied by DH/G); 2:14 is bare ('he took the boy and his mother' — no night, no Egypt), retro-fitted by A and DG. (6) 2:11: the magi open אמתחות — the Joseph-narrative's sack-word (Gen 42-44) — and present a מנחה of gold and frankincense (Lev 2:1-2's pairing); מור is glossed with Latin mira. (7) 2:20 repeats Exod 4:19 ('for those who sought... are dead') — Moshe's recall from Midian. (8) 2:22: Archelaus is called הורקנוס (Hyrcanus), and Yoseph turns to the land of GILGAL (again 4:12) where Greek has Galilee. (9) 2:23's 'he shall be called Nazaret' rests on the Hebrew pun נצר/נזיר (Isa 11:1; Judg 13:5). (10) Fulfillment verbs vary natively — לגמור, נשלם, לקיים — against Greek's single πληρόω. The ms writes ה״ for the Name, א״י for the Land of Israel, and marks foreign names with gershayim (הורוד״וס, ארגי״לאס, מי״רא). Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 3), 13 (Perek 4), and 16 (Perek 5).
